items.text: Subscribers are the fragile check: the latest reading is 0.6 per 1,000 views against a typical 2.8. Across all episodes DesignerTom converts 3.1 per 1,000 views, Dive Club 1.8.
items.recommendation: Add a spoken subscribe ask in the strongest-holding stretch of the next episode. Test different wording per channel: a pinned comment on Dive Club, a mid-show verbal ask on DesignerTom. Compare per 1,000 views afterward.

items.text: Live turnout is softening: the newest peak is 87 against a typical 97.5. E9 peaked at 133 with 109 watching on average, and each viewer stayed 14.2 minutes.
items.recommendation: Test building the next live around E9's shape: guest and viewer-submitted segments, with longer conversations. Run it for one episode and check peak and minutes stayed against the recent run.

items.text: E9 lost 5.2 of every 100 viewers about an eighth of the way in (around 18 minutes). E5 lost 5.3 at a similar point, around 11 minutes. Early exits repeat across finished episodes.
items.recommendation: Test tightening or re-ordering the first quarter hour: move the first guest or demo ahead of host banter, then compare how many leave early next episode. Treat the timing as approximate.

items.text: Chat is the healthiest part: people chatting per 100 viewers is 83.9 against a typical 53.9, and the share staying to the end reads 84.1 against 66.4.
items.recommendation: Protect it: keep reading chat names on air and keep the viewer-submission segments. Run a caller audio check before going live, since LinkedIn viewers on one earlier episode said they couldn't hear the caller.

items.text: Subscribers supply 71.6% of YouTube views, while end screens brought only 19 views and playlists 312.
items.recommendation: Add end screens pointing to the next episode on every upload and group episodes into a playlist. Check next week whether those two surfaces move off near zero.
